analysis:
This PR changes only documentation (docs/provider/cli-reference.md and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md). It bumps the "Last updated" date, adds descriptions of a bounded lifecycle drain and shutdown behavior, and adds a status-line explanation for selected-model memory retry and an enabled_models restart-needed notice. No code, config defaults or deployment settings are changed in the supplied units.

Security-relevant claims examined:
- Drain with no coordinator session: waits 10 s, then finishes with "coordinator acknowledgement: not needed (no coordinator connection)". The doc justifies this because the disconnect already cancelled accepted work. This touches TB-002 and T-010, but it only documents behavior in ProviderLoop.performLifecycleDrain. That source is not in the supplied evidence, so the claim is unverified and there is no basis for a finding.
- Shutdown waits 15 s per model unload and leaves a stuck native retirement to process exit. This relates to T-028 (residual GPU data) and T-029. It is a documented availability and residue-handling behavior whose implementation I could not inspect.
- Selected-model recovery loads or evicts models automatically. It is bounded by the enabled_models filter, Autopilot holds and leases, and the doc explicitly says it does not evict models outside the selection that a request could not load back. This is a documented operator-config boundary, not an authorization change.
- cli-reference.md head text is unchanged in the cache, App Attest, logout and token sections: the cache references (T-041), the worker-qualification passthrough exactly equal to 1, and the logout/unenroll semantics. I observed no weakening of the stated posture, including the 30-minute TTL, the HMAC names, and the "offline local logout is not remote invalidation" caveat (A-008, T-053).

Remaining questions for integration: whether ProviderLoop.performLifecycleDrain, unloadAllModelsForShutdown and the selected-model retry code match the docs, and whether finishing a drain without a coordinator acknowledgement can leave stale routing state. Those sources are outside this batch. The threat model does not need updating for these docs alone.
